svg.text: F Sub-mechanisms (3) — crush, wash and move without sliding
Each panel loops on its own.
source: F-first-principles.md section 6
S13 Mangle ricer
Cooked flesh through the mesh into the pot; skins stay in the fold
(mash, tomato, apple). Fine mesh: wrings grated potato or spinach.
Feasibility M–H
S19 Cryo-crumble

g.text: squeezed: they shatter into flakes < 3 mm
folded sheet (or through a 6 mm grid)

svg.text: No blade, no green smear on a knife; also solves the 3–5 day
shelf life of fresh herbs. Garnish still needs a cut.
Feasibility H for cooked dishes
S37 Flotation wash
Soil sinks to a trap, leaves float out washed; cut pepper seeds pass
a 6 mm screen. Soup vegetables are flushed into the pot by the
recipe's own water. Feasibility M–H
S5 Clamshell

g.text: half closed: scoop for leaves, pasta
closed: ladle and 60 g ball mould

svg.text: Two stainless half-shells on a scissor: one tool replaces tongs,
scoop, ladle and dumpling former.
Feasibility H
S21 Nose transfer

g.text: nose bar withdraws while the belt runs at the
same speed: the item is laid down, no sliding

svg.text: The baker's conveyor peel: picks up or lays down meat slices,
dough sheets, fish, pancakes, lasagne sheets. Dropped over the
nose onto a surface moving the other way, it lands turned over. H
S28 Helix vessel

g.text: reverse: helix carries the pieces out

svg.text: A fixed internal helix (concrete mixer): no tilt actuator, no scraper.
Feasibility H for loose pieces, useless for pastes
